title: Prevent cross-clone task ID collisions with optional shared ID allocation
scope: Add opt-in shared ID allocation for task creation while retaining numeric task IDs. Provide a minimal usable HTTP allocator with durable atomic per-project counters and integrate its reservation protocol into shared creation used by core/standalone, CLI and MCP. Configuration explicitly enables allocation and selects the service URL and stable project key shared across clones; absent/disabled configuration preserves local allocation and performs no network requests. The service reserves and returns an ID rather than merely exposing the last occupied ID. Define the minimal endpoint/configuration contract, service deployment route and authentication during technical design. Keep task records local JSON; the shared service holds only allocation state. This task must deliver a runnable allocator and working multi-clone creation, not just a client for an unspecified future backend.
acceptance: Without enabled shared allocation, existing creation behavior and interfaces remain compatible and make no allocator requests. Enabled configuration validates the endpoint and stable project key; local absolute paths are not used as cross-clone project identity.

Two independent clones configured for the same shared project can create tasks concurrently and receive distinct positive safe-integer IDs; project keys isolate counters. Allocation is an atomic durable reservation and survives service restart.

Provide an explicit safe enrollment procedure that starts above all existing IDs and retained counters across participating clones. Request floors cannot move the shared counter backward; adding an older/offline clone requires reconciliation. Clearly document that unconfigured/offline writers cannot share this uniqueness guarantee.

Retries after lost replies use the same allocation-request identity and cannot accidentally reserve a different ID for that retry. Failed local creation may leave a harmless reserved gap; IDs are not recycled. Allocation idempotency does not falsely claim whole-task-creation idempotency.

When enabled, unreachable/unauthorized service, timeouts, malformed replies, exhausted counters and locally conflicting returned IDs fail clearly without creating a task or silently falling back to local allocation. Explicit-ID creation must not bypass shared uniqueness; define and verify its reservation/rejection behavior.

Authentication credentials remain outside committed project records, request/response sizes and waits are bounded, and endpoint trust/HTTPS requirements are documented. Network waits do not hold the local writer lock; final local validation, blockers, collision checks and write coordination still run safely after reservation.

Exercise the actual runnable allocator and at least two independent project directories through shared creation and affected CLI/MCP boundaries, including concurrency, retry, restart, outage and disabled-mode scenarios. Keep transport behavior and public contracts aligned and pass required CI.

Document minimal service setup, opt-in configuration, safe enrollment, failure handling and the limitation that unique IDs do not automatically resolve Git merges of task JSON. Update the existing local-only product contract to describe the explicitly optional allocation-state service.

values.goal: Keep repository-local JSON tasks usable by developers and agents working in independent clones.
values.value: Participating clones can create tasks with globally distinct project-scoped numeric IDs without manual prefixing or renumbering.
values.observable_result: A runnable shared allocator and opt-in tracker configuration demonstrate concurrent task creation across independent clones without ID collisions.
values.verification: Run concurrent creates against one durable allocator from two separate project directories; verify distinct IDs before/after restart, safe retry/outage behavior and unchanged network-free local mode.

notes: Owner proposed an optional config-controlled address for querying the latest occupied project ID. Refined to atomic reservation because a read-last-then-increment protocol still races between clients.
Existing numeric IDs, blockers and references remain numeric; this task does not adopt composite per-person identifiers.

Choose the smallest deployable service/storage option during technical design. Do not assume a hosting provider or create paid infrastructure from this planning request. Task creation does not start implementation or deployment.

title: Simplify installer completion messages across platforms
scope: Update the packaged Linux, macOS and Windows installer messages and completion behavior. Remove all suggestions to close the window using keyboard shortcuts, including 'If the window stays open, close it with Cmd+W.'. Always display the canonical short command 'outask' in Command; retain the platform-appropriate full executable path with correct quoting in Run immediately for use before a new terminal is opened. End successful installation with 'Installation complete. Open a new terminal to start working.'. Append 'Press any key to finish.' and wait for a key only in launch contexts where the installer window would otherwise close automatically; omit both the prompt and wait when the terminal remains open. Preserve the installed-location line and readable spacing. This task covers completion messages and pause behavior, not update functionality.
acceptance: Successful installation shows 'Installed Outask at <installation path>.', a blank line, 'Command: outask', 'Run immediately: <correctly quoted full executable path> --help', a blank line, and 'Installation complete. Open a new terminal to start working.'.

macOS output uses the actual paths, for example: Installed Outask at /Users/user/Library/Application Support/Outask. followed by Command: outask and Run immediately: '/Users/user/.local/bin/outask' --help, with the agreed blank lines.
No installer message suggests closing the window with Cmd+W or another keyboard shortcut.
'Press any key to finish.' and its key wait are present only for launch contexts where the window otherwise closes automatically. Persistent terminal sessions show neither the prompt nor the wait.

Focused platform installer checks verify final output, short Command, executable-path quoting for paths containing spaces, and pause behavior in automatically closing windows versus persistent terminals; inspect captured successful installation output at the user boundary and run the applicable project gates.
values: Goal: provide usable packaged CLI/MCP installation on supported Linux, macOS and Windows platforms (docs/product.md). Value: users immediately see the short CLI command and a usable immediate-run command, without unnecessary window-closing instructions or key waits. Observable result: the completed installer presents the agreed concise message and pauses only when needed to keep an automatically closing window readable. Verification: inspect successful installer output and exit/pause behavior for automatically closing launches and persistent terminal sessions on the supported platform routes.

title: Publish SHA256SUMS for release archives
scope: Generate and publish a deterministic SHA256SUMS release asset containing SHA-256 checksums and exact filenames for the three accepted platform archives. Hash the final archives actually uploaded, without rebuilding them. Integrate the extra asset into release publication, retry/recovery validation and downloaded-archive acceptance, and provide concise Linux, macOS and Windows verification commands in the existing installation/release documentation. Preserve exact approved notes, existing published releases and Actions-owned publication.
acceptance: Each new release publishes SHA256SUMS with exactly one standard checksum entry for each of its Linux x64, macOS arm64 and Windows x64 archives, using their final uploaded bytes and filenames.

Publication and recovery accept an identical existing checksum asset, upload only missing assets and reject mismatches; partial uploads cannot publish an incomplete or inconsistent release. Existing releases are not rewritten.
Native downloaded-release acceptance verifies each downloaded platform archive against the downloaded SHA256SUMS; a changed archive or invalid/missing checksum entry fails clearly.

Users can follow documented platform-specific verification commands successfully for a matching archive and observe a failure for altered bytes. Explain that checksums verify file integrity and are not a signature of origin.
Focused release-generation, publication and recovery checks plus required CI pass; actual publication/download results are verified read-only after an approved owner merge.
